title: On the structure of low-rank PPT entangled states violating Peres conjecture
abstract: Bound-entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT) can exhibit quantum steering and Bell nonlocality, disproving the long-standing Peres conjecture and its stronger steering counterpart. These counterexamples, obtained through explicit constructions or numerical searches, raise the question of whether they share a common structural origin. We address this question in the low-rank regime by asking whether known counterexamples can be obtained, up to invertible local filtering, from the complement of an unextendible product basis (UPB). We find that the answer depends crucially on the local dimension. In $3\otimes3$, the rank-four structure of PPT entangled states implies that both the steerable PPT state of Moroder \textit{et al.} and the Bell-nonlocal PPT state of Vértesi and Brunner can be obtained from UPB-complement states under invertible local filtering. For three qubits, in contrast, rank-four states that are PPT across every bipartition are separable across each cut. Moreover, comparison of the product-vector structure of the relevant kernels shows that the known three-qubit Bell-nonlocal PPT states cannot be obtained by invertible local filtering from the complement of any three-qubit UPB. Going beyond rank four, we further show that a known rank-eight three-qutrit state, supported on the complement of a UPB and PPT across every bipartition, is genuinely multipartite entangled. These results show that UPBs provide a unifying structural origin for important low-rank PPT entangled states in $3\otimes3$, but that nonlocal bound entanglement is not, in general, a UPB phenomenon.
summary: This theoretical work explores the structural properties of low-rank entangled states that violate the Peres conjecture. By comparing known counterexamples to the complement of Unextendible Product Bases (UPBs), the authors show that while UPBs characterize certain states in $3\otimes3$, they do not provide a universal structural origin for all nonlocal bound entanglement in general.
main_problem: The paper investigates the structural origin of low-rank Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) entangled states that violate the Peres conjecture and exhibit quantum steering or Bell nonlocality.
main_result: The structural origin depends on the local dimension: for $3\otimes3$, UPBs provide a unifying structure for rank-four states, but nonlocal bound entanglement is not generally a UPB phenomenon.
method: The authors use explicit constructions, numerical searches, and comparison of the product-vector geometry of state kernels under invertible local filtering to test structural equivalence.
model_or_system: The study focuses on multipartite quantum states, specifically in the low-rank regime, involving systems of qubits and qutrits ($d=3$). Key concepts include PPT states, Unextendible Product Bases (UPBs), and various forms of entanglement/nonlocality.
key_observables: PPT property, quantum steering, Bell nonlocality, state rank, and structural equivalence under local filtering.
important_parameters: Local dimension (e.g., $3\otimes3$), state rank (e.g., rank-four, rank-eight).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing states via invertible local filtering and characterizing entanglement using the UPB structure.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the structural constraints imposed by the PPT condition on low-rank entangled states, contrasting results for $3\otimes3$ (where UPBs are relevant) versus three qubits (where UPB structure fails to capture all known non-local states).
why_interesting: It provides deep structural insights into the boundary between separable, bound entangled, and genuinely non-local quantum states, which is fundamental to understanding quantum correlations beyond simple entanglement measures.
